title: And Rose Byrne is coming back to Broadway in a couple months! #broadw...
transcript: Ranking all of the 2026 Oscar nominees that I've seen do live theatre. And to be clear, I'm ranking their stage performances, not their nominated film performances. To illustrate that. In last place, I have Elle Fanning, who I actually really like, which is why I was extra disappointed when her performance in Appropriate on Broadway, did not live up to my hopes. She wasn't outright bad, but I thought she was kind of miscast and uneasy on stage. In fifth place, and probably not for the reason you think, I have Jessie Buckley, who I'm also a big fan of. If I saw her in Cabaret, she'd probably be a lot higher on the list, but I saw her in The Winter's Tale opposite Judi Dench and Kenneth Branagh. Nothing really wrong with the performance, it just wasn't that memorable because the role of Perdita is kind of thankless and the production was not that good. In fourth place, Rose Byrne, who I saw in You Can't Take it With You on Broadway and in this adaptation of Medea, where she definitely had a lot more to work with. It was a pretty impressive, very unsettling performance. Kind of inconsistent, though. Like the more heightened dramatic scenes were better, I think, than the more naturalistic scenes. They also used a lot of close up live feed video, and surprisingly, her acting read better from the balcony than it did on camera. I'm sure it's tricky, but I have seen lots of actors calibrate that balance better. In 3rd place, I may not have seen Jessie Buckley as Sally Bowles in cabaret, but I did get to see Emma Stone. her singing wasn't amazing in this role, but she definitely held her own vocally, and more importantly, I thought she acted the role really beautifully with a lot of her natural charisma. In second place, a legit pro, Amy Madigan, who I've seen on stage twice. First in Buried Child. She really skillfully navigated this turn from a kind of mild facade to fiercely protecting her home. I also saw her in this very star studded play, Good for Otto, where she also delivered solid work. But in first place, I have Ethan Hawke, who's done a lot of stage work, but I saw him in True West on Broadway opposite Tarantino's favorite actor, Paul Dano. And they were both very good, but Ethan Hawke, I thought, was really extraordinary, playing this wild, uninhibited character while still feeling totally focused and grounded as an actor.
